notes: Reserve hosts (antigravity, junie) sit between the primary hosts and the floor. Neither is a quality step down -- both reach Claude Opus and Sonnet -- so their position is a BILLING order, not a quality order: flat-rate subscription capacity is spent first because it is already paid for whether used or not, and metered capacity is held back. That is precisely why they sit ABOVE the floor: reaching for equal-quality reserve beats dropping a tier and losing quality. They are absent from cheap commands, where the floor costs little anyway. Ordering between the two reserves is by headroom: antigravity carries a weekly allowance, junie a much tighter 10-20 credits per 30 days. ANTIGRAVITY (Google AI Plus) replaces the deprecated Gemini CLI and holds TWO independent weekly pools -- one for Gemini Flash/Pro, one for Claude Opus/Sonnet/GPT-OSS. Choosing a tier therefore also chooses which pool drains, so an exhausted Claude pool does not block Gemini-model work and vice versa. JUNIE draws JetBrains AI credits (All Products Pack -> AI Pro). On both reserve hosts consumption is proportional to token cost, unlike the flat-rate primaries, so the tier changes spend directly -- Opus-class work drains fast while Gemini Flash Lite or GPT-5.6-LUNA stretch the same budget by roughly 20x. Neither reserve host is in agents.tiers, so their tiers resolve unpinned: the tier is advice about what to select in that tool, not a resolved model. Standalone Gemini CLI is deliberately absent -- it is deprecated in favour of antigravity. See spike-findings.md.

/task.why: Reading an issue and naming a branch is deterministic script execution; no reasoning tier does this better than another.

/grill-with-docs.why: Interrogating a plan for hidden assumptions and coining precise glossary terms is the judgment work that separates tiers; a shallow model produces a shallow grill and the miss is silent.

/speckit-specify.why: Converts an already-settled brief into spec sections; mostly structured transcription once the grill has done the thinking.

/speckit-clarify.why: Surfaces remaining ambiguity as direct questions against a spec that already exists; recognizing a gap is easier than authoring the resolution.

/speckit-plan.why: Architectural reasoning about how a feature gets built; a wrong plan compounds through every later stage, so this is where a silent miss costs the most.

/speckit-tasks.why: Decomposes an approved plan into a task list; largely mechanical once the plan states the shape of the work.

/speckit-analyze.why: Cross-checks spec, plan, tasks, and the constitution for contradictions; catching a subtle inconsistency is exactly the kind of miss that stays silent on a weaker model.

/implement.why: Writes the production code and tests; the highest-token stage and the one where quality variance is most visible, so it anchors the top of the map.

/gherkin.why: Translates settled scenarios into Gherkin; opt-in stage with moderate reasoning and a small, checkable surface.

/refactor.why: Reduces complexity and duplication against numeric gate thresholds; the target is measurable, so the model mainly needs to satisfy a check it can verify itself.

/code-review.why: Three-axis diff review; the risk axis (security, concurrency, coverage gaps) needs real judgment even though standards and spec checks are closer to a checklist.

/architect.why: Interprets Stryker survivors and decides whether the invariant or the test is wrong; a mistaken call here either hides a real gap or adds a test that proves nothing.

/ship-review.why: Final pre-PR fan-out; high stakes for what it gates but review-only and checklist-heavy, so balanced clears it without deep's cost.
